title: Margherita pizza
intro: Tomato, mozzarella and basil on a tall, airy crust, even in a home oven.

steps.t: Heat the oven to max (250-280 °C) with a pizza stone or upturned tray on the top shelf, for 45 minutes.
steps.label: Oven

pan.t: Turn the broiler to max and heat a 28 cm cast-iron skillet over high heat for 10 minutes.

steps.t: Meanwhile, crush the tomatoes by hand and season with salt and a little oil. Dice the mozzarella and let it drain.
Stretch a dough ball (store-bought is fine) with your fingertips from the center out, leaving a 1 cm rim.
Spread 3 tbsp of tomato, slide the pizza onto the stone on its baking paper and bake for 4 minutes.
steps.label: Stone

pan.t: Lay the pizza in the hot skillet, spread the tomato and cook for 2-3 minutes, until the base is spotted.

steps.t: Add the mozzarella and finish under the broiler for 3-4 minutes, until the crust is puffed and spotted.
steps.label: Broil

pan.t: Add the mozzarella and slide the skillet under the broiler, close to the element, for 2-3 minutes, until puffed.

steps.t: Take it out, top with basil and a drizzle of olive oil. Repeat with the other dough balls.

tips.t: Drain the mozzarella in the fridge for a few hours so the pizza doesn't turn soggy.
Skip the mozzarella and add sliced garlic and oregano for a marinara.

title: Sfincione palermitano
intro: Palermo's thick, soft pizza with onion sauce, anchovies, caciocavallo and crumbs.

steps.t: Oil a 30x40 cm pan with 2 tbsp of oil, stretch the dough (store-bought is fine) to the edges, cover and let it rise for 1 hour.
steps.label: In the pan

steps.t: Meanwhile, thinly slice the onions and stew them in 3 tbsp of oil over low heat for 15 minutes, until soft.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Add the crushed tomatoes, salt and pepper and cook for 20 minutes, until thick.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220 °C. Press the chopped anchovies and half the caciocavallo, diced, into the risen dough.
Cover with the onion sauce, pushing it well into the corners.
Toast the breadcrumbs in a pan with a little oil, then mix with the oregano and the rest of the caciocavallo, grated.
Scatter them on top, drizzle with the remaining oil and bake on the lowest rack for 30 minutes, until the edges are crisp.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it cool for 10 minutes and cut into squares.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: It's just as good cold the next day, the way Palermo's street vendors sell it.
Skip the anchovies and add more caciocavallo for a version kids love.

title: Calzone
intro: Neapolitan folded pizza filled with ricotta, mozzarella and salami, baked or fried.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 250 °C with a baking sheet inside. Drain the mozzarella well and dice it.

fry.t: Heat the sunflower oil to 175 °C in a deep pot. Drain the mozzarella well and dice it.

steps.t: Mix the ricotta, mozzarella, diced salami, parmesan and some black pepper.
Stretch a dough ball (store-bought is fine) by hand into a 25 cm disc.
Put a quarter of the filling on one half, fold into a half-moon and seal the edge by pressing with your fingers.
Brush with a spoonful of passata and a little oil, then cut a small slit on top to let steam escape.

fry.t: Don't brush or slit it: seal the edge well so it stays closed in the oil.

steps.t: Bake on the hot sheet for 15 minutes, until puffed and golden.
steps.label: Bake

fry.t: Fry one calzone at a time for 5 minutes, turning, until golden and puffed; drain on paper towels.

steps.t: Let it rest for 5 minutes before cutting: the filling is scalding.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Drain the ricotta in a sieve for 30 minutes so the filling doesn't soak the dough.
Swap the salami for sautéed escarole with olives and capers, as Naples does on Christmas Eve.

title: Roman pizza bianca
intro: Rome's white pizza: just olive oil and coarse salt, crisp underneath and soft inside.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 250 °C (conventional) with a rack on the lowest shelf.
Turn the dough (store-bought is fine) onto a floured surface and press it into a rectangle with your fingertips.
Move it to a 30x40 cm pan greased with 2 tbsp of oil and stretch it to the edges without crushing the bubbles.
Cover and let it rest in the pan for 30 minutes, until slightly puffed.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Brush with the remaining oil, sprinkle with coarse salt and press in dimples with your fingers.
Bake on the lowest rack for 18-20 minutes, until golden on top and crisp underneath.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Take it out, brush with a last drizzle of oil and cut into strips.

tips.t: In Rome it's split while warm and filled with mortadella, or with figs and prosciutto in summer.
Add rosemary needles and paper-thin potato slices for potato and rosemary pizza.

title: Manakish za'atar
intro: Lebanese flatbreads brushed with za'atar and olive oil, fragrant and crisp-edged.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 250 °C with a baking sheet inside. Mix the za'atar and oil into a loose paste.

pan.t: Mix the za'atar and oil into a loose paste; you won't need the oven.

steps.t: Divide the dough (store-bought is fine) into 8 balls and let them rest, covered, for 15 minutes.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Stretch each ball into a 15 cm disc and press in lots of dimples with your fingers.
Spread a spoonful of za'atar paste over each disc, leaving a small border.
Bake on the hot sheet for 6-7 minutes, until the edges are golden and the base crisp.
steps.label: Cook

pan.t: Cook in a covered nonstick pan over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, until the base is golden.

steps.t: Serve hot with tomato, sliced cucumber and mint leaves.

tips.t: With labneh and olives, it's the classic breakfast from Beirut's bakeries.
Make half with za'atar and half with akkawi or crumbled feta: the classic combo.

title: Pizza fritta montanara
intro: Naples' little fried pizzas: puffy dough topped with tomato and parmesan.

steps.t: Simmer the crushed tomatoes with the olive oil, garlic and salt for 15 minutes, until thick.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Meanwhile, divide the dough (store-bought is fine) into 8 balls and stretch them into 10-12 cm discs, 5 mm thick.
Heat the sunflower oil to 175 °C in a deep pot and turn the oven on to 220 °C.
Fry one disc at a time for 1 minute per side, until puffed and golden, then drain on paper towels.
steps.label: Fry

steps.t: Top with a spoonful of sauce and parmesan, then bake for 3 minutes, until the cheese melts.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Finish with a basil leaf and serve right away, piping hot.

tips.t: Test the oil with a scrap of dough: it should float straight up, sizzling.
Skip the sauce and toss them warm in sugar for a sweet treat kids love.
